title: Lighter palak paneer
summary: Restaurant palak paneer is mostly cream. This one gets its body from the spinach itself and finishes with yogurt - same dish, half the calories.

ingredients.note: Where the cream would have gone. Off the heat, or it splits.

steps: Boil a pan of water. Drop the spinach in for 90 seconds, then straight into cold water. Blanching like this keeps it bright green - if you just cook it down it goes army-drab.
Squeeze the spinach out and blend it with the green chillies to a coarse puree. Leave some texture; a completely smooth puree tastes like baby food.
Sear the paneer cubes in half the ghee over high heat until golden on two sides, then lift them out. Optional but worth it.
Same pan, remaining ghee, crackle the cumin. Onion for 5 minutes until soft and light gold.
Ginger and garlic for a minute, then the tomato and powdered spices. Cook until the tomato breaks down and the oil separates, about 5 minutes.
Add the spinach puree and salt. Simmer 5-6 minutes - no longer, or the colour goes. Add a splash of water if it is too thick.
Return the paneer, simmer 2 minutes. Turn the heat OFF, then stir in the yogurt, garam masala, crushed kasuri methi and lemon.
tips: Yogurt into a boiling pan will curdle every time. Off the heat, always.
Soak the seared paneer in warm salted water for 5 minutes before adding it - it goes soft again instead of staying squeaky.
Tofu works in place of paneer for a vegan version; use oil for the ghee and coconut cream for the yogurt.
health_notes: The usual restaurant version runs on 100 ml of cream and a lot of butter. Blanched spinach plus a few spoons of Greek yogurt gets you the same body with roughly half the calories and more protein.

source.adapted: Classic palak paneer, cream replaced with Greek yogurt and the ghee cut to one tablespoon.
